title: Customer Needs Adventure
welcome_lead: Happy customers = happy business. Let's listen to what they want. 💛
meta_desc: Customers & Markets Adventure 2 — KS3 Business Studies on understanding and meeting customer needs.
final_note: You learned how to identify customer needs and the difference between needs and wants.

concepts.def: Customers who buy again and again
Help given once the sale is over

walkthroughs.body_html:
A need is something you must have — food, shelter, school bag.

A want is something nice to have — a designer bag.

Businesses sell both, but they sell them differently.

Customers come in with expectations: quick service, kind staff, fair price.

If the experience beats expectations → high satisfaction.

If it falls short → unhappy customer, bad review.

It costs 5x more to find a new customer than to keep an old one.

Build loyalty with:

  • Good after-sales service.
  • Loyalty cards (Costa, Nando's).
  • Friendly staff who remember you.

Loyal customers come back. 💛

mcqs.q: What does Maslow's hierarchy of needs propose about motivation?
options: Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Maslow said employees must be promoted every year.
Humans are motivated by a hierarchy of needs (physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation) — lower needs must be substantially met before higher ones motivate.
Maslow said money is the most important motivator at work.

mcqs.q: Why are hygiene factors and motivators not on the same scale in Herzberg's theory?
options: Hygiene factors only prevent dissatisfaction (their absence demotivates, presence is neutral); motivators create satisfaction (their presence motivates, absence is neutral). They affect different outcomes, not different points on one scale.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Hygiene factors and motivators are just two types of motivation that combine.

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
Maslow said employees must be promoted every year.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
